title: Civil penalty authority for reporting and programme failures
definition: The authority to impose a civil monetary penalty for a violation of a reporting, recordkeeping or anti-money-laundering programme requirement, and the separate authority to impose penalties on a financial institution for a programme failure, which are assessed against a set of factors including the size of the institution, the duration of the failure and whether it was self-reported. The existence of the penalty authority is why a control failure is a supervisory matter and not only an operational one. This record summarises the authority.
evidence_to_cite: the control that failed, and the period the failure covered
the self-assessment and remediation steps taken, with their dates
the regulatory correspondence, where there is any
